title: I replaced Google Search on my phone to get instant answers without scrolling through ads
excerpt: Getting answers shouldn't be this convoluted
content_html:
Published Aug 14, 2026, 11:30 AM EDT

Akshay Bhalla was the former game guides editor for Screen Rant and the technology editor at MensXP. He has previously written about smartphones, apps, streaming, gadgets and games for print, digital, and TV media outlets. When he isn’t writing about tech, he can often be found playing JRPGs, listening to music or playing with his three dogs.

It seems like searching for anything on Google and getting a prompt answer these days is becoming a nightmare to navigate.

It doesn't matter what I'm trying to look up; my phone's screen is instantly occupied by ads, AI overviews, and useless features.

After dealing with a lot of frustration with Google Search, I decided to change my entire browsing experience.

I replaced Google Search in more than one way

You're never short of alternatives

After I realized a simple Google Search is not the experience it once was, it was time to de-Google my experience.

Google Search prefers to show ads and sponsored clutter on top of the page instead of answering the query promptly.

Do a simple Google search, and your top page will be dominated by product listings that brands aggressively advertise.

It ruined the whole experience for me, as websites with more reliable information I needed weren't prioritized.

For example, I was looking up a guide for a game. Instead of showing me the relevant link, I was shown a product listing for the game from Japan.

On top of being bombarded with ads, Google likes to interject AI overviews that often contain inaccurate or outdated information.

Combine this experience on a smartphone screen, and all of a sudden you don't have any real estate left. With less real estate on my screen when using Google Search, I've often tapped links by accident that I never intended to visit.

This would have a spiraling effect, as I would be bombarded with ads for that product on different websites for the next few days.

There's also the question of privacy, since Google likes to build a profile for every user; it makes me feel like a product rather than a customer.

I use my phone one-handed, and the UX on Google Search is downright abysmal.

Not only do I have to navigate through ads and sponsored posts, but I also have to deal with other necessary features like the People also ask section.

No, Google, I really don't care what other people are asking. Just give me the information I need!

There's also the question of privacy, since Google likes to build a profile for every user; it makes me feel like a product rather than a customer.

After much frustration, it was time to cut off the noise.

The easiest way for me to circumvent Google's practices was to switch search engines. I chose DuckDuckGo as it offered a simpler experience, the way Google Search used to be.

When I have simple queries, DuckDuckGo gives me cleaner results with links to reliable websites I can check for myself. Since there are no ads, DuckDuckGo doesn't build a profile for users.

There are no product listings or sponsored posts to navigate around. The search engine also respects my privacy; it doesn't store my IP address, search history, or personal details.

For once, the search engine felt useful again.

Thanks to DuckDuckGo's privacy policies, every user gets the same search result when using the same keywords rather than being reduced to an ad profile.

Google has a habit of manipulating search results based on your ad profile, which sometimes can feel scummy.

With DuckDuckGo, I don't have to worry about that.

DuckDuckGo offers AI features like AI Mode, but they are optional and not turned on by default.

While I admit Google has a broader index for providing information, DuckDuckGo is no slouch.

The search engine does not rely on one source and, to my surprise, uses Bing to give relevant information.

It felt like the Google Search I used in the mid-2000s, which, most of the time, is all I need today.

Don't Forget Gemini

I will be the first one to admit that Google Search also has its advantages, especially if you are looking to buy something for the best price.

I can understand if someone is not willing to give up Google Search. In such cases, we don't have to look beyond Google to get answers for simple queries.

When I want a quick answer, I often use the AI Mode found in the upper-left corner when using Google Search.

When I was setting up my Synology NAS (Network Attached Storage), I needed quick answers to set up networking settings, Tailscale, and Jellyfin.

I relied heavily on Google's AI Mode and Gemini to get answers, as they are stripped of everything I complained about earlier. It pulled most of the information from XDA, and to my surprise, it wasn't outdated.

There are no ads, sponsored clutter, or unnecessary features I have to navigate around.

In Gemini/AI Mode, I got the answer in a matter of seconds and set up my Synology faster than digging through different websites.

Word of caution, though: AI Mode and Gemini can sometimes give conflicting answers, which isn't ideal for fact-checking.

But for basic queries, it does an excellent job.

Switching your browser might be the answer

I use better browsers than Chrome

If you still use Chrome as the main browser on your phone, you won't escape from ads even if you switch your search engine.

Most websites use some form of advertising, and some have annoying pop-ups that I couldn't block on Chrome.

Unlike Chrome, many alternate Android browsers have built-in ad-blocking features that you shouldn't ignore.

Many of these browsers also respect your privacy and are based on Chromium. So I highly recommend using them if you've used Chrome over the years.

Browsers like Brave, Aloha, or DuckDuckGo's browser are great alternatives, and they have desktop versions that sync effortlessly with the mobile browser.

These browsers also don't track your browsing, which can be a godsend if you spend a lot of time browsing and looking up random things.

Browsers like Brave have their own search engines and have similar offerings like DuckDuckGo.

For Chrome users, switching to Brave is the ideal solution, as it feels right at home without all the tracking.

Since many new browsers are based on Chromium, they support transferring your bookmarks and other details from Chrome to make the switch easier.

I made the switch a long time ago and never looked back.

I don't regret leaving Google Search behind

Leaving Google Search behind was the best decision I made when I wanted quick answers.

It's been two years since I made the switch, and my devices no longer feel like an ad profile that Google wants to sell to. It may not be the most perfect setup, but it gets the job done.

Using an open source browser like Brave or Aloha in tandem with DuckDuckGo feels more liberating, simpler, and more efficient, like Google Search's good old days used to be.

发布于 2026 年 8 月 14 日，美国东部时间上午 11:30

Akshay Bhalla 是 Screen Rant 的前游戏指南编辑和 MensXP 的技术编辑。 他之前曾撰写过有关印刷、数字和电视媒体的智能手机、应用程序、流媒体、小工具和游戏的文章。 当他不写科技文章时，经常会发现他在玩日式角色扮演游戏、听音乐或和他的三只狗玩耍。

如今，在谷歌上搜索任何内容并立即得到答案似乎已经成为导航的噩梦。

我想查找什么并不重要；我的手机屏幕立即被广告、人工智能概览和无用功能占据。

在经历了 Google 搜索的诸多挫折之后，我决定改变我的整个浏览体验。

我以不止一种方式替换了 Google 搜索

你永远不缺少替代品

当我意识到简单的 Google 搜索不再是以前的体验后，是时候对我的体验进行去谷歌化了。

Google 搜索更喜欢在页面顶部显示广告和赞助的杂乱内容，而不是立即回答查询。

进行简单的谷歌搜索，您的首页将被品牌积极宣传的产品列表所占据。

它毁了我的整个体验，因为我需要的包含更可靠信息的网站没有被优先考虑。

例如，我正在查找游戏指南。 我没有看到相关链接，而是看到了来自日本的游戏的产品列表。

除了广告轰炸之外，谷歌还喜欢插入人工智能概述，这些概述通常包含不准确或过时的信息。

将这种体验结合到智能手机屏幕上，突然之间您就没有任何剩余空间了。 使用 Google 搜索时，由于屏幕上的空间较少，我经常会无意中点击我从未打算访问的链接。

这会产生螺旋式的效应，因为接下来的几天里我会在不同的网站上收到该产品的广告轰炸。

还有隐私问题，因为谷歌喜欢为每个用户建立个人资料。这让我感觉自己是一个产品而不是客户。

我单手使用手机，谷歌搜索的用户体验非常糟糕。

我不仅必须浏览广告和赞助帖子，而且还必须处理其他必要的功能，例如“人们还询问”部分。

不，谷歌，我真的不在乎其他人在问什么。 只要给我我需要的信息就可以了！

还有隐私问题，因为谷歌喜欢为每个用户建立个人资料。这让我感觉自己是一个产品而不是客户。

经过一番挫败之后，是时候切断噪音了。

对我来说，规避谷歌做法的最简单方法就是切换搜索引擎。 我选择 DuckDuckGo，因为它提供了更简单的体验，就像 Google 搜索过去的方式一样。

当我有简单的查询时，DuckDuckGo 会为我提供更清晰的结果，并提供我可以自己检查的可靠网站的链接。 由于没有广告，DuckDuckGo 不会为用户建立个人资料。

没有可供浏览的产品列表或赞助帖子。 搜索引擎也尊重我的隐私；它不会存储我的 IP 地址、搜索历史记录或个人详细信息。

这一次，搜索引擎再次变得有用。

得益于 DuckDuckGo 的隐私政策，每个用户在使用相同的关键字时都会获得相同的搜索结果，而不是被简化为广告配置文件。

谷歌有根据你的广告资料操纵搜索结果的习惯，这有时会让人感觉很糟糕。

有了 DuckDuckGo，我就不用担心这个问题了。

DuckDuckGo 提供 AI 模式等 AI 功能，但它们是可选的，默认情况下不打开。

虽然我承认 Google 有更广泛的索引来提供信息，但 DuckDuckGo 也毫不逊色。

令我惊讶的是，该搜索引擎并不依赖于单一来源，而是使用 Bing 来提供相关信息。

这感觉就像我在 2000 年代中期使用的 Google 搜索，而在大多数时候，这就是我今天所需要的。

别忘了双子座

我将是第一个承认 Google 搜索也有其优势的人，特别是如果您想以最优惠的价格购买东西。

如果有人不愿意放弃 Google 搜索，我可以理解。 在这种情况下，我们不必通过 Google 之外的方式来获取简单查询的答案。

当我想要快速得到答案时，我经常使用 Google 搜索时左上角的 AI 模式。

当我设置 Synology NAS（网络附加存储）时，我需要快速找到设置网络设置、Tailscale 和 Jellyfin 的答案。

我严重依赖谷歌的人工智能模式和双子座来获得答案，因为它们剥夺了我之前抱怨的所有内容。 它从 XDA 中提取了大部分信息，令我惊讶的是，它并没有过时。

没有广告、赞助商的混乱或我必须浏览的不必要的功能。

在 Gemini/AI 模式下，我在几秒钟内就得到了答案，并且比浏览不同网站更快地设置 Synology。

不过，请注意：AI 模式和 Gemini 有时会给出相互矛盾的答案，这对于事实检查来说并不理想。

但对于基本查询，它做得非常出色。

切换浏览器可能是答案

我使用比 Chrome 更好的浏览器

如果您仍然使用Chrome作为手机上的主要浏览器，即使您切换搜索引擎，您也无法摆脱广告。

大多数网站都使用某种形式的广告，有些网站有令人讨厌的弹出窗口，我无法在 Chrome 上阻止。

与 Chrome 不同，许多替代 Android 浏览器都具有您不应忽视的内置广告拦截功能。

其中许多浏览器也尊重您的隐私并且基于 Chromium。 因此，如果您多年来一直使用 Chrome，我强烈建议您使用它们。

Brave、Aloha 或 DuckDuckGo 等浏览器都是不错的选择，它们的桌面版本可以轻松与移动浏览器同步。

这些浏览器也不会跟踪您的浏览，如果您花费大量时间浏览和查找随机内容，这可能是天赐之物。

像 Brave 这样的浏览器有自己的搜索引擎，并且有类似的产品，比如 DuckDuckGo。

对于 Chrome 用户来说，切换到 Brave 是理想的解决方案，因为它感觉就像在家里一样，无需所有跟踪。

由于许多新浏览器都基于 Chromium，因此它们支持从 Chrome 传输书签和其他详细信息，以便更轻松地进行切换。

我很久以前就做出了转变，并且再也没有回头。

我并不后悔放弃 Google 搜索

当我想要快速得到答案时，放弃 Google 搜索是我做出的最佳决定。

自从我做出改变以来已经两年了，我的设备不再感觉像谷歌想要出售的广告配置文件。 它可能不是最完美的设置，但它可以完成工作。

将 Brave 或 Aloha 等开源浏览器与 DuckDuckGo 结合使用感觉更自由、更简单、更高效，就像 Google 搜索过去的美好时光一样。
